sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Sorting arrays is like organizing your closet - it makes everything easier to find! Let's learn how to arrange numbers or words in order.

• How to sort arrays in ascending/descending order
• Built-in Java sorting methods
• How sorting works behind the scenes

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you have a messy pile of numbered cards. Sorting is like arranging them from smallest to largest number.

• Sorting puts elements in a specific order (numbers: 1,2,3... or words: A,B,C...)
• Java has built-in tools to sort arrays automatically
• You can sort numbers, strings, or even custom objects

Think of it like organizing your music playlist by song title or your contacts by name - it makes everything more useful!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Selection sort finds the minimum element and swaps it into the correct position each pass
Insertion sort builds the sorted portion one element at a time by shifting larger elements
Both selection sort and insertion sort have O(n^2) time complexity
Arrays.sort() uses a highly optimized sorting algorithm and should be preferred in practice
Understanding sorting algorithms builds intuition for algorithm efficiency

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Sorting organizes array elements in order (numbers or words) `Arrays.sort()` is your best friend for quick sorting. Practice sorting different types of data. Ready to learn about searching sorted arrays next.

questions.question: What is the basic idea behind selection sort?
options: Insert each element into its correct position
Find the minimum element and swap it to the front, then repeat
Divide the array and sort each half
Compare adjacent elements and swap them
questions.explanation: Selection sort works by repeatedly finding the minimum element from the unsorted portion and placing it at the beginning of that portion.

questions.question: What method can be used to sort an array using Java's built-in library?
questions.explanation: Arrays.sort(arr) from the java.util.Arrays class sorts the array in ascending order. It uses an optimized sorting algorithm internally.
